definitions.explanation: A Japanese form of massage in which the practitioner applies pressure with the fingers, thumbs, and palms to specific points on the body. Often used to relieve muscle stiffness ({肩|かた}こり) and fatigue. Sometimes paired with する as a verb.

examples.japanese: {肩|かた}を{指圧|しあつ}してもらった。
examples.english: I had my shoulders massaged with shiatsu.

examples.japanese: {指圧|しあつ}{師|し}に{腰|こし}を{治療|ちりょう}してもらう。
examples.english: To have a shiatsu therapist treat my lower back.

examples.japanese: {長時間|ちょうじかん}のデスクワークで{凝|こ}り{固|かた}まった{肩|かた}を、{指圧|しあつ}で{丁寧|ていねい}にほぐしてもらった。
examples.english: I had my shoulders, stiffened from long hours of desk work, carefully loosened with shiatsu.

notes:
Compound of {指|ゆび}/{指|し} ("finger") + {圧|あつ} ("pressure"). A traditional Japanese therapeutic practice that draws on Chinese medicine theory of meridians and pressure points but developed into a recognized profession in early-20th-century Japan. Practitioners are licensed nationally as {あん{摩|ま}マッサージ{指圧|しあつ}{師|し}}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {指圧|しあつ}する: to give a shiatsu massage
- {指圧|しあつ}を{受|う}ける: to receive a shiatsu treatment
- {指圧|しあつ}{師|し}: shiatsu practitioner
- {指圧|しあつ}{療法|りょうほう}: shiatsu therapy

SIMILAR WORDS:
- マッサージ: massage — generic term; includes shiatsu, oil massage, etc.
- {整体|せいたい}: chiropractic-like body adjustment — focuses on skeletal alignment
- {鍼灸|しんきゅう}: acupuncture and moxibustion — uses needles and heat, not pressure
